{{Field procedure|summary=Launch and read a prospector limpet before committing mining time, ammunition or collector capacity to an asteroid.}}

A prospector limpet analyses one mineable asteroid. After it attaches, targeting the limpet displays the asteroid's contents, remaining ordinary resources and any exposed deposits, sub-surface deposits, fissures or core resource. For laser mining, prospecting before extraction also increases the number of fragments available; the controller rating determines that increase.<ref name="prospector">[https://elite-dangerous.fandom.com/wiki/Prospector_Limpet_Controller Prospector Limpet Controller], ''Elite Dangerous Wiki''. Accessed 16 September 2026.</ref>

The prospector identifies what is inside the selected asteroid. It does not locate a profitable market, search an entire ring or decide whether a result fits the current run.

== Before you start ==

* Fit and power a [[Prospector Limpet Controller]], assign it to a fire group and carry limpets in the cargo hold.
* Decide what the run is seeking: ordinary laser-mined composition, surface deposits, sub-surface deposits or a core.
* Use the appropriate search method before prospecting. A [[Detailed Surface Scanner]] reveals ring hotspots, while a [[Pulse Wave Analyser]] helps locate anomalous candidates for deposit and core mining. Neither replaces the prospector's asteroid-scale report.<ref name="frontier">[https://forums.frontier.co.uk/threads/content-recap-beyond-chapter-four-livestream-mining-and-squadrons.454587/ Content Recap: Beyond — Chapter Four Livestream — Mining and Squadrons]. Frontier Developments, 1 November 2018. Accessed 16 September 2026.</ref>
* Approach within the controller's range and leave a clear path between the ship and the candidate asteroid.

== Procedure ==

{{Procedure steps|
# Select a candidate asteroid using the ring, hotspot and search method appropriate to the intended commodity.
# Enter Analysis Mode and align the ship so the limpet's path does not cross another asteroid or a fast-moving projection on the target.
# Fire one prospector at the asteroid. Each launch consumes one limpet from cargo.
# Wait for the limpet to strike and attach, then target the attached prospector.
# Read the target-information panel. Check the ordinary commodity percentages and resources remaining, then look for any listed surface deposits, sub-surface deposits, fissures or core resource.
# Compare the result with the objective set for the run. There is no universal percentage threshold: the useful minimum depends on the commodity, travel time, extraction method and commander's priorities.
# If the asteroid is unsuitable, launch at another candidate. If it is suitable, keep its result available while positioning for the appropriate extraction procedure.
}}

For [[Laser Mining|laser mining]], attach the prospector before firing mining lasers. The fragment-yield increase is not retroactive, so fragments removed first do not receive the later bonus.<ref name="prospector" /> An A-rated dedicated controller provides the highest documented laser-fragment multiplier; the full rating table belongs to [[Prospector Limpet Controller]].

== Reading the result ==

* '''Commodity percentages''' identify the ordinary resources available to mining lasers. They do not report sale prices or guarantee a profitable trip.
* '''Resources remaining''' tracks the ordinary laser-minable supply. It is not a measure of unworked surface deposits, sub-surface deposits or fissures.
* '''Surface and sub-surface deposits''' become targetable for an [[Abrasion Blaster]] or [[Sub-surface Displacement Missile]].
* '''Fissures and core resource''' confirm a core asteroid and identify the targets used by a [[Seismic Charge Launcher]].
* '''Material content''' describes the asteroid's potential raw Engineering-material output; raw materials use material storage rather than refinery bins or cargo racks.

== Managing active prospectors ==

A controller supports only a limited number of active prospectors. Launching another after that limit is reached expires the oldest one. Do not replace the prospector attached to an asteroid still being worked if its result or deposit markers are needed.<ref name="prospector" />

Higher controller classes can keep more prospectors active and may have greater range. Rating affects the laser-fragment multiplier and other module characteristics. Check the fitted module rather than assuming that every dedicated or multi-limpet controller behaves identically.

== Common problems ==

* '''The limpet misses or breaks:''' reduce ship motion, align with a broad face of the asteroid and avoid firing across nearby rock. Rotation can move a projection into the flight path after launch.
* '''The controller will not fire:''' verify module power, the active fire group, Analysis Mode, limpet stock and controller range.
* '''A result disappears after another launch:''' the controller reached its active-prospector limit and expired the oldest limpet.
* '''No useful composition appears:''' the asteroid does not match the run's target. Move on rather than spending extraction time and collector capacity on it.
* '''A deposit tool has nothing to target:''' confirm that the prospector reports the matching deposit type. A bright Pulse Wave return alone does not provide the deposit targets.
* '''Laser yield is lower than expected:''' attach the prospector before extraction and verify the controller rating. The module's class number is not the documented yield multiplier.
